about: Crash text patterns for alloy.report.LogDiagnosis. First matching 'cause' entry is the headline when the built-in rules found nothing specific; 'first' entries are checked before the built-in rules; 'note' entries are only extra lines. lines: error = skip matches on INFO, DEBUG, TRACE and WARN log lines, warn = WARN lines count too, any = every line counts. {N} in cause and fix is regex group N, {N|text} uses text when group N is empty. unless: the entry is skipped when this matches anywhere; when: the entry is only checked when this matches somewhere; replaces: ids whose hits this entry's hit removes.

signatures.pattern: Attempted to load class (\S+) for invalid dist DEDICATED_SERVER|Attempting to load a clientside only mod
signatures.cause: A client-only mod is installed on a dedicated server{1| (it tried to load the client class {1})}.
signatures.fix: Remove that mod from the server (forgemods/ or mods/) and keep it on the client only. The class name shows which mod it is.

signatures.pattern: Cannot load class (\S+) in environment type SERVER
signatures.cause: A Fabric mod loaded the client class {1} on a dedicated server, so it is a client-only mod.
signatures.fix: Remove that Fabric mod from the server's mods/ folder and keep it on the client.

signatures.pattern: IllegalAccessError: (?:class|failed to access class) (\S+) \(in (?:module|unnamed module of loader) [^)]+\) cannot access (?:class )?(\S+) \(in module ([^)]+)\) because module \S+ does not (?:export|open)
signatures.cause: Code in {1} was blocked from using {2} because the Java module {3} does not open that package to it. This is a module access problem, not a wrong mod version.
signatures.fix: Send the bundle to the Alloy developer. To play now, remove the mod that owns {1}.

signatures.pattern: requires compatibility level (JAVA_\d+) which is not (?:supported|available)
signatures.cause: A mod's code patches need Java compatibility level {1}, which this Java or this Mixin version does not support.
signatures.fix: Start the game with a newer Java (see the version the mod asks for), or update the mod's loader libraries.

signatures.pattern: zip END header not found|zip file is empty|ZipException: (?:invalid (?:CEN|LOC) header|error in opening zip file)|File (\S+) is not a jar file|Failed to create secure jar for|UnionFileSystem\$UncheckedIOException
signatures.cause: A mod jar is damaged or is not a jar at all{1| ({1})}. This usually comes from a download that stopped early.
signatures.fix: Download that mod again. Run Mod Doctor to find which jar cannot be opened.

signatures.pattern: IOException: (?:There is not enough space on the disk|No space left on device)
signatures.cause: The disk is full, so the game could not write its files.
signatures.fix: Free some disk space and start the game again.

signatures.pattern: Could not reserve enough space for (?:\d+KB )?object heap|Invalid maximum heap size
signatures.cause: Java could not get the amount of memory set for the game. Either this is a 32-bit Java, or more memory was asked for than the PC has.
signatures.fix: Use a 64-bit Java and set a smaller maximum memory (for example 4 GB) in your launcher.

signatures.pattern: Mod ID: '(?:minecraft|forge|neoforge)', Requested by: [^\n]*?, Actual version: '\[MISSING\]'|Error loading class: net/minecraft/world/level/biome/Biome \(java\.lang\.IllegalStateException: Unable to find method
signatures.cause: Forge cannot find Minecraft or itself among the loaded mods, so the install is damaged.
signatures.fix: Run the Alloy installer again for this game folder; it rebuilds the prepared game files.

signatures.pattern: Could not execute entrypoint stage 'main' due to errors, provided by 'mcd[\s\S]{0,4000}?ClassNotFoundException: com\.blamejared\.clumps\.api\.
signatures.cause: MC Dungeons Weapons or Armors (Fabric build) needs the Fabric build of Clumps, but only the Forge Clumps is installed.
signatures.fix: Put the Fabric Clumps jar in mods/, or use the Forge builds of the MC Dungeons mods.

signatures.pattern: ClassCastException: class net\.minecraft\.world\.item\.ItemStack cannot be cast to class io\.github\.apace100\.apoli\.access\.EntityLinkedItemStack
signatures.cause: Medieval Origins needs the Fabric build of Origins, but the Forge port of Origins is installed.
signatures.fix: Put Fabric Origins in mods/ and remove the Forge Origins from forgemods/, or use an older Medieval Origins.

signatures.pattern: (?<![(\w.$])(?:java\.lang\.)?ClassNotFoundException: net\.caffeinemc\.mods\.sodium\.api\.memory\.MemoryIntrinsics|(?<![(\w.$])(?:java\.lang\.)?NoClassDefFoundError: net/caffeinemc/mods/sodium/api/vertex/buffer/VertexBufferWriter|(?<![(\w.$])(?:java\.lang\.)?ClassNotFoundException: me\.jellysquid\.mods\.sodium\.client\.render\.immediate\.model\.ModelPartData
signatures.cause: Oculus is installed without Embeddium (or with Rubidium, which is not enough: Oculus 1.7 and newer use Embeddium classes that Rubidium does not have).
signatures.fix: Install the Embeddium version Oculus asks for, in forgemods/.

signatures.pattern: (?<![(\w.$])(?:java\.lang\.)?(?:ClassNotFoundException|NoClassDefFoundError): (com[./]simibubi[./]create[./](?!foundation[./]ponder[./]PonderWorld\b)\S+|com[./]jozufozu[./]flywheel\S*|dev[./]engine_room[./]flywheel\S*|net[./]createmod\S*)
signatures.cause: A Create addon was made for another major version of Create (Create 6 moved many classes; {1} is missing).
signatures.fix: Use builds of every Create addon that match the installed Create version, or remove the addon named in the stack trace.

signatures.pattern: (?<![(\w.$])(?:java\.lang\.)?(?:ClassNotFoundException|NoClassDefFoundError): (yesman[./]epicfight\S*)
signatures.cause: An Epic Fight addon was made for another Epic Fight version ({1} is missing).
signatures.fix: Use builds of the Epic Fight addons that match the installed Epic Fight version.

signatures.pattern: (?<![(\w.$])(?:java\.lang\.)?(?:ClassNotFoundException|NoClassDefFoundError): (mod[./]azure[./]azurelib\S*)
signatures.cause: A mod was made for another major version of AzureLib ({1} is missing).
signatures.fix: Install the AzureLib version that mod was made for (see its download page).

signatures.pattern: ClassMetadataNotFoundException: ((?:net[./]minecraft[./]client|com[./]mojang[./]blaze3d)[./][\w.$/]+)
signatures.when: ModLauncher launch target: forge_server|net\.minecraft\.server\.Main\.main\(|KnotServer|Starting minecraft server version|dist=DEDICATED_SERVER
signatures.cause: A mod on this dedicated server has a code patch for the client class {1}, so it is a client-only mod (or a mod whose client part is in the server's folder).
signatures.fix: Remove client-only mods from the server's mods/ and forgemods/ folders and keep them on the client. The mixin config named above the error shows which mod it is.

signatures.cause: Controlify adds its sounds after Forge has locked the game's registries, so it does not start on Alloy yet (seen with Zoomify and Controlify in Fabulously Optimized).
signatures.fix: Start without Controlify: crash recovery offers to turn it off on the next start (or run the installer with --disable-mod, the game folder and controlify). Turn it back on any time with --restore-disabled. The rest of the pack keeps working, only controller support is missing.
signatures.source: run/b053 final check, Fabulously Optimized 5.4.1 on 1.20.1 (Controlify 1.6.0+1.20, ControlifySounds.register)

signatures.pattern: Cannot invoke "me\.jellysquid\.mods\.sodium\.client\.model\.quad\.properties\.ModelQuadFacing\.ordinal\(\)" because "(?:facing|face)" is null
signatures.cause: Sodium 0.5 (often pulled in by Indium) cannot draw Forge's block models: on Minecraft 1.21.x Alloy's Sodium fixes are made for Sodium 0.6 and newer, so the first chunk with a Forge-built model crashes.
signatures.fix: On Minecraft 1.21.x: install Sodium 0.6 or newer (0.6.13 or 0.8.x for 1.21.1) and remove Indium, which only exists for Sodium 0.5 (Sodium 0.6 has the Fabric rendering API built in). On 1.20.x: keep alloy-sodium120.jar in mods/ next to Sodium 0.5.

signatures.cause: Fabric mod {1} tried to add blocks or items after Forge locked the game's registries. Alloy normally lets Fabric mods register their content, so this is a bug for the Alloy developer (or the mod registers later than Fabric mods should).
signatures.fix: To play now, start without {1}: run the installer with --disable-mod, the game folder and the mod id from the mod list (for example controlify; see When the game crashes in INSTALL.md). Please send the crash report bundle (--report) to the Alloy developer. If your Alloy is older than the newest release, update it first.
signatures.source: Alloy regression run on 1.21.1, crash report before the fix

signatures.pattern: IllegalStateException: Item group has no page
signatures.cause: The creative inventory crashed because a Fabric mod's creative tab got no page number. This was an Alloy bug on 1.20.1, fixed in current Alloy.
signatures.fix: Update Alloy to the newest build and run its installer on this instance again. If it still happens on the newest build, send the crash report bundle to the Alloy developer. To play now, remove the Fabric mod that adds its own creative tab.
signatures.source: Alloy regression run on 1.20.4, crash reports

signatures.pattern: No candidates were found matching (?:field_1658|f_90810_|MAP):Ljava/util/Map; in net/minecraft/(?:client/KeyMapping|class_304)(?: for ([\w.\-]+\.json))?|NoSuchFieldError: (?:Class net\.minecraft\.client\.KeyMapping does not have member field 'java\.util\.Map (?:MAP|f_90810_)'|(?:field_1658|f_90810_)\b)|ClassCastException: class net\.minecraftforge\.client\.settings\.KeyMappingLookup cannot be cast to class java\.util\.Map
signatures.cause: A Fabric mod{1| ({1})} reads Minecraft's key binding map (KeyMapping.MAP), which Forge replaced with its own type, so the mod cannot start on Alloy yet.
signatures.fix: Remove that mod for now, or use its Forge build if it has one. Known cases: Amecs on 1.20.1 and KeybindsGalore Plus on 26.x.

signatures.pattern: (?i)OptiFineTransformationService|\bOptiFine[_ ]1\.\d+(?:\.\d+)?[_ ]HD|\bOptiFine[_ ]HD[_ ]U|\boptifabric-[\w.+\-]*\.jar|OptiFine present \(unsupported override\)
signatures.cause: OptiFine is installed. It replaces Minecraft's rendering code in a way Fabric API, Forge rendering mods and Alloy cannot work with, so crashes that name other mods are often caused by it.
signatures.fix: Remove OptiFine (and OptiFabric), even when allowUnsupported.optifine is set. Use Embeddium with Oculus on Forge 1.20.1, or Sodium with Iris on Fabric. If the game still crashes, the next crash report shows the real cause.

signatures.pattern: (?<![(\w.$])(?:java\.lang\.)?(?:NoSuchMethodError|NoClassDefFoundError|NoSuchFieldError|ClassNotFoundException):? [^\n]*?net[./]fabricmc[./]fabric[./]impl[./]([\w./$]+)
signatures.cause: A mod uses internal code of Fabric API (net.fabricmc.fabric.impl.{1}) that the installed Fabric API does not have.
signatures.fix: Put the Fabric API version the mod was made for (or newer) in mods/, or update the mod. Using these internals is the mod's choice, so tell its author too.

signatures.pattern: imgui\.extension\.texteditor\.TextEditorLanguageDefinition|NoSuchMethodError: [^\n]*\bimgui\.
signatures.cause: Two mods bring different copies of the imgui library (for example Axiom and Veil), and the copy that loaded first is missing parts the other needs.
signatures.fix: Update Veil (or the mod that bundles it, such as Sable or Create Aeronautics) and Axiom, or remove one of them.

signatures.pattern: Mod file ([\w.+\-]+\.jar) has failing mixins:
signatures.cause: This game runs Sinytra Connector, which stopped because Fabric mod {1} has code patches that failed.
signatures.fix: Alloy does not need Connector. Remove Connector, Connector Extras and Forgified Fabric API from forgemods/ and put the real Fabric API in mods/.

signatures.pattern: Timed out waiting for jar remap
signatures.cause: This game runs Sinytra Connector, which timed out while converting Fabric jars at startup.
signatures.fix: Alloy converts Fabric mods when it installs them, so this cannot happen on Alloy. Remove Connector, Connector Extras and Forgified Fabric API from forgemods/.

signatures.pattern: NoSuchMethodError: [^\n]*connector\$redirect\$
signatures.cause: This game runs Sinytra Connector, and a Fabric mod's code patch calls a helper Connector did not create.
signatures.fix: Remove Connector, Connector Extras and Forgified Fabric API from forgemods/ and put the real Fabric API in mods/.

signatures.cause: A code patch (mixin) of mod {2} could not be applied ({1}).
signatures.fix: Update {2} or remove it. If it works on plain Forge or plain Fabric, the clash is with a mod from the other loader.

signatures.pattern: Mixin \[([\w.\-]+\.json):([\w.$]+)\] from phase \[\w+\] in config \[[\w.\-]+\.json\] FAILED during (APPLY|PREPARE|POST_APPLY)
signatures.cause: The code patch {2} from {1} failed while it was being applied ({3} step).
signatures.fix: Update or remove the mod that owns {1}. Run Mod Doctor if you are not sure which jar that is.

signatures.pattern: @Shadow (?:field|method) (\S+) was not located in the target class (\S+)
signatures.cause: A mod's code patch expects {1} in {2}, but it is not there. The mod was made for another Minecraft version, or Forge changed that code.
signatures.fix: Update the mod to its build for this Minecraft version, or remove it.

signatures.pattern: ClassMetadataNotFoundException: ([\w.$/]+)
signatures.cause: A mod's code patch refers to class {1}, which no installed mod has. Usually a mod it needs is missing or has another major version.
signatures.fix: Install the right version of the mod that owns {1}, or remove the mod that needs it.

signatures.pattern: The specified resource '([\w./\-]+\.json)' was invalid or could not be read
signatures.cause: A mod's code patch file {1} is missing or broken inside its jar.
signatures.fix: Download that mod again. If the jar is fine on plain Forge or Fabric, send the bundle to the Alloy developer.

signatures.pattern: LVT in ([\w/$.]+)::([^\s(]+)\S* has incompatible changes at opcode (\d+) in callback(?: ([\w.\-]+\.json):([\w.$]+))?
signatures.cause: A mod's code patch ({4|a mixin}) expected other local variables in Minecraft's {1} method {2}. Forge changed that method, so the patch does not fit.
signatures.fix: Update the mod that owns {4|that mixin} and Fabric API. If it still happens, use the Forge build Alloy lists as tested and send the crash report bundle to the Alloy developer.

signatures.pattern: Critical injection failure: (?:Callback method|@\w+ annotation on) (\S+) in ([\w.\-]+\.json):([\w.$]+)[^\n]*?failed injection check, \((\d+)/(\d+)\) succeeded
signatures.cause: A mod's code patch {2}:{3} found {4} of the {5} places it must change in Minecraft's code. Forge or another mod changed that code first.
signatures.fix: Update the mod that owns {2}, or remove it. If it works on plain Fabric or plain Forge, the clash is with a mod from the other loader or with Forge itself.

signatures.pattern: MixinTargetAlreadyLoadedException(?:: [^\n]*?target ([\w.$]+) was loaded too early)?
signatures.cause: Minecraft's class {1|(see the log)} was loaded before the mods that patch it were ready, so their code patches could not be applied.
signatures.fix: Remove the mod you added last (the stack trace under the error shows what loaded the class early) and send the crash report bundle to the Alloy developer.

signatures.pattern: Itemstack (\d+) ([\w.\-]+:[\w./\-]+) does not exist in tab's list
signatures.cause: A mod tried to place items in a creative tab next to {2}, which is not in that tab. Two mods, or the Fabric and Forge tab systems, changed the same tab.
signatures.fix: Update the mods that add items to that tab (Architectury mods, tab editing mods). If it only happens with Fabric mods installed, send the crash report bundle to the Alloy developer.

signatures.pattern: Accidentally adding the same item stack twice ([^\n]+?) to a Creative Mode Tab: ([^\n]+)
signatures.unless: Failed to collect creative tab|Item Group crashed while building contents
signatures.cause: Item {1} was added twice to the creative tab {2}, which the game does not allow. Often a mod adds it once through Fabric and once through Forge.
signatures.fix: Update the mod that owns that item. If it is a Fabric mod that works on plain Fabric, send the crash report bundle to the Alloy developer.

signatures.pattern: (?:No registration for payload|Unknown custom packet payload:) ([\w.\-]+:[\w./\-]+)
signatures.cause: Network message {1} arrived on a side where no mod registered it. The mod is missing on one side, or its registration did not reach the other loader.
signatures.fix: Install the mod that owns {1} on both the server and the client, in the same version. If it is on both, send the crash report bundle to the Alloy developer.

signatures.pattern: This server requires ([^\n(]+?) \(unhandled packet: ([\w.\-]+:[\w./\-]+)\)
signatures.cause: The server needs {1}, which this client could not use (packet {2}).
signatures.fix: Install {1} on the client, in the server's version. If it is installed, the mod's network setup did not reach the other loader: send the crash report bundle to the Alloy developer.

signatures.pattern: Payload ([\w.\-]+:[\w./\-]+) may not be sent to the (server|client)!
signatures.cause: A mod tried to send network message {1} to the {2}, which does not know it, and the loader refused instead of dropping it.
signatures.fix: Install the mod that owns {1} on both sides. If it is on both, update that mod.

signatures.pattern: Failed decoding custom payload ([\w.\-]+:[\w./\-]+)
signatures.cause: Network message {1} could not be read, usually because the server and the client have different versions of that mod.
signatures.fix: Use the same version of the mod that owns {1} on the server and the client.

signatures.cause: Network channel {1} was registered twice, often once through Fabric API and once through the other loader.
signatures.fix: Check that the mod that owns {1} is installed once (not its Forge and Fabric builds together). If it is, send the crash report bundle to the Alloy developer.

signatures.pattern: ClassCastException: class net\.fabricmc\.fabric\.impl\.networking\.payload\.PacketByteBufLoginQueryResponse
signatures.cause: A proxy forwarding mod (for Velocity) and Fabric's networking both answered the same login query.
signatures.fix: Use legacy forwarding on the proxy, or a forwarding mod that knows about Fabric login queries.

signatures.pattern: No model for layer ([\w.\-]+:[\w./\-]+)#(\w+)
signatures.cause: The entity model {1}#{2} was missing when the game built its models. A Fabric mod's client setup can run before Forge mods have added their models; the mod named here is often not the cause.
signatures.fix: Start the game again (it depends on timing). If it keeps happening, remove the Fabric mod you added last and send the crash report bundle to the Alloy developer.

signatures.pattern: Registry not present in RegistryOps|Can't (?:access|find) registry ResourceKey\[minecraft:root / ([\w.\-]+:[\w./\-]+)\]
signatures.cause: World or data pack data uses the registry {1|of a mod}, which was not set up when the data was read. The mod registered it too late.
signatures.fix: Update the mod that adds that registry (its name is the part before the colon). If it is a Fabric mod that works on plain Fabric, send the crash report bundle to the Alloy developer.

signatures.pattern: IllegalAccessError: (?:class \S+ )?tried to access (private|protected) (field|method) ([\w.$]+)
signatures.cause: Code tried to use the {1} {2} {3}, which is still {1} when the game runs. The mod that opens it up was made for another version, or Forge replaced that member.
signatures.fix: Update the mod named in the stack trace. If it works on plain Fabric, send the crash report bundle to the Alloy developer.

signatures.pattern: No RecipeManager found in listeners!
signatures.cause: Fabric API could not find Minecraft's recipe loader among the data reload steps, because another mod or the server software changed that list.
signatures.fix: Remove the mod or server software that replaces reload listeners (for example a Sponge based server), or send the crash report bundle to the Alloy developer.

signatures.pattern: Cannot convert flowing fluid ([\w.\-]+:[\w./\-]+) \([^)]*\) into a still fluid
signatures.cause: Fabric's fluid transfer was given the flowing fluid {1}; the Forge mod that owns it does not mark its source fluid as a source.
signatures.fix: Update the mod that owns {1}. If it still happens, send the crash report bundle to the Alloy developer.

signatures.pattern: ClassCastException: class ([\w.$]+BakedModel[\w$]*) cannot be cast to class ([\w.$]+)
signatures.cause: A render mod wrapped the block model {1}, and another mod expected its own model class {2}.
signatures.fix: Turn off model wrapping for those blocks (Continuity settings or its resource pack), or remove one of the two mods.

signatures.pattern: java\.lang\.VerifyError: (Bad type on operand stack|Bad local variable type|Inconsistent stackmap frames|Bad access to protected data|Operand stack overflow|Expecting a stackmap frame)[^\n]*
signatures.cause: Java refused to run a class because its code is broken ({1}). Two mods changing the same method, or a mod made for another version, cause this.
signatures.fix: The Location line under the error names the class. Remove the mod you added last, or send the bundle to the Alloy developer.

signatures.pattern: java\.lang\.LinkageError: loader constraint violation[^\n]*
signatures.cause: The same class was loaded twice by different loaders and the two copies clashed. Usually a library is installed twice.
signatures.fix: Look for a library that is both bundled inside a mod and installed on its own, and remove the extra copy. If none, send the bundle to the Alloy developer.

signatures.pattern: (?:LinkageError|IllegalStateException)[^\n]*(?:attempted\s+)?duplicate class definition for:? ?([\w/$.]+)
signatures.cause: Class {1|in the message} is provided twice, so it could not be loaded.
signatures.fix: Find the two jars that contain it and remove one. A library bundled in both a Forge mod and a Fabric mod is the usual cause.

signatures.pattern: java\.lang\.ClassCircularityError: ([\w/$.]+)
signatures.cause: Loading class {1} needed that same class again, so it could not load. A mod's loading plugin is usually behind this.
signatures.fix: Remove the mod you added last. If that does not help, send the bundle to the Alloy developer.

signatures.pattern: SecurityException: class \"?([\w.$]+)\"?'s signer information does not match signer information of other classes in the same package
signatures.cause: Class {1} comes from a signed jar, but another jar has classes in the same package. One of them was repacked or both ship the same code.
signatures.fix: Remove the jar that duplicates that package.

signatures.pattern: SecurityException: Invalid signature file digest for Manifest main attributes
signatures.cause: A jar was changed after it was signed, so Java refuses its signature.
signatures.fix: Download the mod again. If a tool repacked it, use the original jar.

signatures.pattern: ResolutionException: (?:Modules (\S+) and (\S+) export package (\S+) to module (\S+)|Module (\S+) contains package (\S+), module (\S+) exports package \S+ to)
signatures.cause: Two jars provide the same Java package, so Forge cannot start. Usually the same library or mod is installed twice.
signatures.fix: Keep only one jar with that package. For MixinExtras, keep the newest one.

signatures.pattern: FindException: Module (\S+) not found, required by (\S+)
signatures.cause: Module {1} is not installed, but {2} needs it.
signatures.fix: Install the library that provides {1}, or remove {2}.

signatures.pattern: Mod ID: '([\w-]+)', Requested by: '([\w-]+)', Expected range: '([^']*)', Actual version: '([^']*)'
signatures.cause: Forge mod {2} needs {1} {3}, but the installed version is {4}.
signatures.fix: Install or update {1} to a version in that range (in forgemods/), or remove {2}.

signatures.pattern: (?i)net\.neoforged:forge:1\.20\.1-47\.1\.\d+|neoforge-47\.1\.\d+
signatures.cause: This pack uses NeoForge's old 1.20.1 build instead of Forge 47.
signatures.fix: Alloy runs real Forge 47 for 1.20.1; import the pack again and do not add NeoForge.

signatures.pattern: Some intrusive holders were not (?:registered|added to registry): \[([^\]]*)\]
signatures.cause: A mod created game objects that were never registered: {1}.
signatures.fix: This is usually a knock-on error: fix the first error above it in the log first. Otherwise update or remove the mod that owns those objects.

signatures.pattern: Registry Object not present: ([\w.-]+:[\w./-]+)
signatures.cause: A mod asked for {1}, which was never registered. Usually the mod that adds it is missing, turned off in a config, or differs between client and server.
signatures.fix: Check that the mod named before the colon in {1} is installed, on both client and server, with the same config.

signatures.pattern: Trying to access unbound value '?ResourceKey\[([\w:./-]+) / ([\w:./-]+)\]'?
signatures.cause: Game data refers to {2} ({1}), which no installed mod or data pack provides.
signatures.fix: Install the mod named before the colon in {2}, or remove the data pack or mod that refers to it.

signatures.pattern: Unbound values in registry ResourceKey\[minecraft:root / ([\w:./-]+)\]: \[([^\]]*)\]|Missing key in ResourceKey\[minecraft:root / ([\w:./-]+)\]: ResourceKey\[[^\]]+\]
signatures.cause: World generation data refers to entries that no installed mod defines: {2|see the log}.
signatures.fix: Install the mods named before the colons, or check whether one of them failed to load earlier in the log.

signatures.pattern: IllegalStateException: Feature order cycle found|FeatureCycleDetector\$FeatureCycleException: A feature cycle was found
signatures.cause: Two world generation mods place the same features in a different order, so the game cannot sort them.
signatures.fix: Remove or reconfigure one of the world generation mods. The mod Cyanide can name the features that clash.

signatures.pattern: IllegalStateException: Failed to parse (.+) from pack file/(.*)
signatures.cause: A data file could not be read: {1} in {2}.
signatures.fix: Fix or remove that data pack. If the file is inside a mod jar, update that mod.

signatures.pattern: IllegalStateException: Failed to parse [^\n]* from pack KubeJS Resource Pack \[data\]
signatures.cause: A KubeJS data file in kubejs/data is broken.
signatures.fix: Fix the named file in kubejs/, or install the pack again.

signatures.pattern: ResourceLocationException: Non \[a-z0-9(?:/\._-|_\.-)\] character in (?:path|namespace) of location: (\S+)
signatures.cause: A resource or data file has a name with a capital letter, space or other character the game does not allow: {1}.
signatures.fix: Rename it to lower case without spaces, or remove the resource pack or data pack that has it.

signatures.pattern: ExecutionException: .+ Overworld settings missing
signatures.cause: The world has no overworld settings. A world generation mod or data pack it was made with is gone, or level.dat was edited.
signatures.fix: Install the world generation mod or data pack the world was made with again.

signatures.pattern: Run the command /fml confirm or (?:or )?/fml cancel to proceed\.
signatures.cause: The world has blocks or items from mods that are not installed now, and the Forge server waits for a decision before removing them.
signatures.fix: Install the missing mods again, or back up the world and then run /fml confirm.

signatures.pattern: ConfigLoadingException: Failed loading config file (\S+\.toml) of type SERVER for modid (\S+)
signatures.cause: The world's server config {1} of mod {2} is broken (often empty after a crash or power cut).
signatures.fix: Delete that file in the world's serverconfig folder; the mod writes a new one.

signatures.pattern: ConfigLoadingException: Failed loading config file (\S+\.toml) of type (CLIENT|COMMON) for modid (\S+)
signatures.cause: The config file {1} of mod {3} cannot be read (empty, damaged, or a typo after editing).
signatures.fix: Delete or fix {1} in config/. The mod writes a new one with default settings.

signatures.pattern: Cannot get config value before config is loaded
signatures.cause: A mod read one of its settings before Forge had loaded the config files.
signatures.fix: This is a bug in that mod: update it or report it to its author. If it works on plain Forge, send the bundle to the Alloy developer.

signatures.pattern: FileSystemException: (.+): The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process
signatures.cause: Another program has the file {1} open: a second game, an editor, a sync tool or an antivirus.
signatures.fix: Close the other game or program and start again.

signatures.pattern: Caused by: java\.lang\.NoClassDefFoundError: Could not initialize class com\.sun\.jna\.
signatures.cause: The JNA library could not load its native part. This often happens when the launcher was installed as administrator.
signatures.fix: Install the launcher again without administrator rights, or use another launcher.

signatures.pattern: IllegalArgumentException: Malformed \\uxxxx encoding\.
signatures.cause: server.properties has a backslash that is not valid (often in a Windows path or the MOTD).
signatures.fix: Fix or remove the line with the backslash in server.properties.

signatures.pattern: ConcurrentModificationException[\s\S]{0,3000}?(?:DeferredWorkQueue|ModLoadingContext|FMLModContainer|ModWorkManager|EventBus)
signatures.cause: A mod changed shared game data from a loading step that runs on several threads at once.
signatures.fix: Start the game again; it often works the second time. Report it to the mod named in the stack trace.

signatures.pattern: ConcurrentModificationException[\s\S]{0,1500}?DistanceManager
signatures.cause: Chunk loading tickets changed while the server was going through them. Chunk loader and world generation mods can cause this.
signatures.fix: Update the chunk loading mods. This is not caused by a missing mod.

signatures.pattern: A single server tick took ([\d.]+) seconds \(should be max 0\.05\)
signatures.cause: The server stopped because one tick took {1} seconds (it hung).
signatures.fix: The thread dump under it shows the stuck code; the first mod in the 'Server thread' stack is the one to update or remove.

signatures.pattern: Payload may not be larger than (?:1048576|32767|2097152) bytes|Packet too big|(?<!for fix \")Badly compressed packet
signatures.cause: A network packet was bigger than the game allows. Big modded inventories or recipe lists in large packs cause this.
signatures.fix: Install a packet size mod on both sides (for example Packet Fixer).

signatures.pattern: Tried to read NBT tag that was too big; tried to allocate: (\d+) ?bytes where max allowed: (\d+)
signatures.cause: An item or block has more data than the network limit allows (tried {1} bytes, the limit is {2}). Often an overfilled backpack or storage block.
signatures.fix: Install Packet Fixer on both sides, or empty that container.

signatures.pattern: (?i)mismatched mod channel list|Mod rejections|Channels \[[^\]]*\] rejected
signatures.cause: Client and server have different networked mods or mod versions.
signatures.fix: Make the mods on both sides match. On Alloy this includes the Fabric mods in mods/.

signatures.pattern: Failed to read from https://api\.minecraftservices\.com/publickeys due to Connect
signatures.cause: The server could not reach Mojang's login service (firewall, DNS or an outage).
signatures.fix: Check the network connection or wait. This is not a mod problem.

signatures.pattern: \*\*\*\* FAILED TO BIND TO PORT!
signatures.cause: The server port is already in use, often by an old server that is still running.
signatures.fix: Stop the other server, or set another server-port in server.properties.

signatures.pattern: You need to agree to the EULA in order to run the server
signatures.cause: The server stopped because the Minecraft EULA is not accepted yet.
signatures.fix: Read the EULA (https://aka.ms/MinecraftEULA) and set eula=true in eula.txt.

signatures.pattern: NullPointerException: No fabric renderer found|Cannot invoke \"net\.fabricmc\.fabric\.api\.renderer\.v1\.Renderer\.meshBuilder\(\)\" because the return value of \"net\.fabricmc\.fabric\.api\.renderer\.v1\.RendererAccess\.getRenderer\(\)\" is null
signatures.cause: A Fabric mod uses the Fabric rendering API, but no renderer is active.
signatures.fix: On Fabric Sodium below 0.6, install Indium. Otherwise send the bundle to the Alloy developer.

signatures.pattern: UnsupportedOperationException: A mod tried to access the state neighbor table directly
signatures.cause: A mod reads block state data that FerriteCore removes to save memory.
signatures.fix: Set populateNeighborTable = true in FerriteCore's config, and report it to the mod named in the stack trace.

signatures.pattern: Simple Clouds does not currently support shaders with Distant Horizons
signatures.cause: Simple Clouds stops when Distant Horizons and a shader mod are both installed.
signatures.fix: Remove one of Simple Clouds, Distant Horizons or the shader mod (Oculus or Iris).

signatures.pattern: doesn't contains VLC binaries for your OS and ARCH
signatures.cause: WaterMedia needs VLC, which it does not bring for this system.
signatures.fix: Install VLC, or remove WaterMedia and the mods that need it.

signatures.pattern: GLFW error 6554[23]|WGL: The driver does not appear to support OpenGL|Pixel format not accelerated
signatures.cause: No working OpenGL graphics driver was found (missing GPU driver, basic display driver, or a remote desktop session).
signatures.fix: Install the graphics driver from your GPU maker (Nvidia, AMD or Intel). This is not a mod problem.

signatures.pattern: #\s+C\s+\[nvoglv64\.dll
signatures.cause: Java crashed inside the Nvidia graphics driver.
signatures.fix: Do a clean reinstall of the Nvidia driver. If you use shaders, try without them.

signatures.pattern: #\s+C\s+\[atio6axx\.dll
signatures.cause: Java crashed inside the AMD graphics driver.
signatures.fix: Do a clean reinstall of an AMD driver that is known to work with Minecraft.

signatures.pattern: #\s+C\s+\[(ig7icd64|ig75icd64|igxelpicd64|igxe2hpgicd64)\.dll
signatures.cause: Java crashed inside the Intel graphics driver ({1}).
signatures.fix: Update the Intel driver. On a laptop with a second GPU, set javaw.exe to use that GPU.

signatures.pattern: #\s+C\s+\[glfw\.dll
signatures.cause: Java crashed in GLFW, the window library, usually because of the graphics driver.
signatures.fix: Update the graphics driver and turn off overlays (Discord, recording tools).

signatures.pattern: #\s+C\s+\[jemalloc\.dll
signatures.cause: Java crashed in the jemalloc memory allocator that LWJGL uses.
signatures.fix: Add the JVM argument -Dorg.lwjgl.system.allocator=system in your launcher.

signatures.pattern: #\s+V\s+\[jvm\.dll
signatures.cause: Java itself crashed (inside jvm.dll). This can be a Java bug or unstable RAM or CPU (overclocking, XMP, some Intel 13th and 14th gen CPUs).
signatures.fix: Update Java. Turn off overclocking or XMP and run a memory test.

signatures.pattern: ~StubRoutines::SafeFetch32
signatures.cause: This Java build crashes on Apple Silicon Macs.
signatures.fix: Use another Java build, for example Eclipse Temurin or Azul Zulu.

signatures.cause: Java crashed in the graphics driver during a draw call that Sodium and Embeddium use.
signatures.fix: Update the graphics driver. Report it with your GPU model to the renderer mod.

signatures.pattern: libasyncProfiler\.so
signatures.cause: spark's profiler crashed Java.
signatures.fix: Update spark, or set spark's profiler engine to java in its config.

signatures.pattern: (?i)exit ?code:? ?-1073741819|EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION
signatures.cause: Java crashed in native code (graphics driver, LWJGL or another native library), so the Java error in the log is not the cause.
signatures.fix: Read the hs_err_pid file in this bundle (Problematic frame line). Updating the graphics driver fixes most of these.

signatures.pattern: IllegalStateException: (?:Not building!|Already building!|Not filled all elements of the vertex)
signatures.cause: A render mod left the drawing buffer in a wrong state ({0}). This is often a second error after an earlier one.
signatures.fix: Look for an earlier error in the log. Otherwise update or remove the render mod named first in the stack trace.

signatures.pattern: IllegalStateException: Pose stack not empty
signatures.cause: A renderer did not clean up after drawing (pose stack not empty), often an entity renderer after an earlier error.
signatures.fix: Look for the entity or renderer in the crash details. With Pehkui, the mod No More Pose Crash helps.

signatures.pattern: This world was saved with mod (?!(?:forge|minecraft) )(\w+) which appears to be missing, things may not work well
signatures.cause: The world was saved with mod {1}, which is not installed now. Its blocks and items will be lost.
signatures.fix: Install {1} again, or back up the world before playing on. Check that it did not move from forgemods/ to a Fabric build with another id.

signatures.pattern: Could not execute entrypoint stage '([^']+)' due to errors, provided by '([\w-]+)'
signatures.cause: Fabric mod {2} failed while starting (its {1} step). The real error is the first Caused by line under it.
signatures.fix: Update {2} or remove it from mods/.

signatures.cause: A code patch (mixin) of mod {1} broke while being applied.
signatures.fix: Update {1} or remove it. The Caused by line says what went wrong.

signatures.pattern: Errors in element ([\w:./-]+) for registry ResourceKey\[[^\]]+\]|Failed to load registries due to above errors
signatures.cause: The world's data could not be loaded{1| (first bad entry: {1})}. The lines above it in the log hold the real errors.
signatures.fix: Fix or remove the data pack or mod named in the first 'Errors in element' line.

signatures.pattern: (?m)^Description: Ticking entity$|^-- Entity being ticked --$
signatures.cause: An entity crashed while it was updated. This repeats every time its chunk loads. The 'Entity Type' line in the crash report names the mod.
signatures.fix: Update or remove that mod. To get into the world, the mod Neruina can skip the broken entity.

signatures.pattern: (?m)^Description: Ticking block entity$
signatures.cause: A block entity crashed while it was updated. The 'Name' and 'Block location' lines in the crash report say which one and where.
signatures.fix: Update or remove the mod that adds that block. Neruina, or removing the block with a world editor, gets you back in.

signatures.pattern: Caught exception from ([^\(\n]+) \(([\w-]+)\)
signatures.cause: Forge mod {1} ({2}) threw an error during loading.
signatures.fix: Update {2} or remove it from forgemods/.

signatures.cause: Forge mod {3} ({1}, file {4}) is marked as errored in the crash report's mod list.
signatures.fix: Update {3} or remove it from forgemods/.

signatures.pattern: This world was saved with mod (\w+) version (\S+) and it is now at version ([^,]+), things may not work well
signatures.cause: Mod {1} changed from version {2} to {3} since the world was saved. Usually harmless.
signatures.fix: If the crash names {1}, try its old version.

signatures.pattern: Missing data pack mod:([\w-]+)
signatures.cause: The world's data pack list names mod {1}, which is not installed now.
signatures.fix: Install {1} again if the world needs it; otherwise its data is dropped.

signatures.pattern: IntegratedWatchdog[^\n]*A single server tick has taken
signatures.cause: One game tick took very long (ModernFix's watchdog). Not a crash by itself, but often the last clue before a freeze.
signatures.fix: The stack it prints names the mod that was busy.

signatures.pattern: Embeddium instance tainted by mods: \[([^\]]*)\]
signatures.cause: These mods change Embeddium: {1}. A crash in Embeddium code is most often caused by one of them.
signatures.fix: Try without those mods first.

signatures.pattern: (?i)\brubidium-mc1\.20\.1-[\w.+-]*\.jar|\brubidium@
signatures.cause: Rubidium is installed. It is no longer maintained and has known bugs; Embeddium replaces it.
signatures.fix: Replace Rubidium with Embeddium (and Oculus 1.6.15 or newer).

signatures.pattern: (?i)\bctov-[\w.+-]*\.jar
signatures.cause: ChoiceTheorem's Overhauled Village is installed without Lithostitched. It breaks once other world generation mods are present.
signatures.fix: Install Lithostitched.

signatures.pattern: (?i)\bgeckoanimfix\b
signatures.cause: 'Iris/Oculus and GeckoLib Compat' is installed. Current GeckoLib does not need it and it is known to crash.
signatures.fix: Remove it.

signatures.pattern: (?i)\birlandacore\b
signatures.cause: Irlanda Core is installed. It has a chat command that gives its author creative mode on any server that runs it.
signatures.fix: Remove it, especially from a server.

signatures.pattern: (?i)\b(sodium|iris|lithium)-[\w.+-]*fabric[\w.+-]*(?<!-alloy)(?<!-forgefab)\.jar
signatures.cause: The Fabric build of {1} is installed next to Forge mods.
signatures.fix: Run Mod Doctor: it says whether this build works on Alloy, or points to the Forge build (Embeddium, Oculus or Radium).

signatures.pattern: AL lib: \(EE\) alc_cleanup: 1 device not closed
signatures.cause: The sound library reported a device that was not closed at exit. This is usually harmless.
signatures.fix: Only look at this if nothing else explains the crash; some setups need a larger start memory (-Xms2G).

signatures.pattern: Creative Tab Loop Found
signatures.cause: Forge found creative tabs that are each sorted before the other, so some tabs are left out of the creative inventory.
signatures.fix: Update Zeta and Quark if installed. If tabs are still missing, send the crash report bundle to the Alloy developer.
